_: PRE-REGISTERED round 2. Written before any round-2 measurement except phase-A discovery, which is enumeration rather than prediction and is recorded as a finding (F1) not a verdict. Never edited after the first run.
why: Round 1 was asymmetric by design: it tested OpenAI's headline feature (semantic_vad, 45 trials) and Gemini's headline risks (barge bug, EU, reseed). Gemini never faced the trail-off fixtures, no generation/endpointing split existed for either vendor, no barge-in tested a long reply, and OpenAI's latency carried a silence_duration_ms the harness chose. Round 2 closes those gaps so the recommendation rests on symmetric evidence.

findings_already_measured.finding: europe-west2 (London) serves NO Gemini Live model. Every candidate fails the WebSocket upgrade with an HTTP 400 from the Google frontend; the bidi path is not routed in that region. europe-west1 (Belgium) and us-central1 serve exactly one: gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio. AI Studio serves only gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview.
findings_already_measured.consequence: There is exactly ONE production-viable Gemini candidate: gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio on Vertex europe-west1. The 3.1 preview measured in round 1 is AI-Studio-only, which is neither a residency nor a BAA surface. A UK-data-stays-in-the-UK promise cannot be met by Gemini Live at all.

verdicts.prediction: At its most patient VAD setting (END_SENSITIVITY_LOW, silenceDurationMs 1200), Gemini holds BOTH no_terminal_punct and trailing_lead_in in >=4 of 5 — i.e. it beats OpenAI, which failed trailing_lead_in at every eagerness.
verdicts.fails_if: either fixture is held in <=3 of 5 — Gemini has the same endpointing weakness and neither vendor solves our measured failure case

verdicts.prediction: At Gemini's DEFAULT VAD — the setting every round-1 number was measured with — it cuts into trailing_lead_in in >=3 of 5.
verdicts.fails_if: <=2 — the default is already patient and W1's tuning is unnecessary

verdicts.prediction: With automatic VAD disabled and an explicit activityEnd, Gemini's pure generation time (activityEnd -> first audio) p50 is < 700 ms.
verdicts.fails_if: >= 700 ms — Gemini's speed advantage is endpointing, not generation, and OpenAI's ~790 ms generation is competitive

verdicts.prediction: At silence_duration_ms=200, OpenAI mini's model leg p50 drops below 1,500 ms — confirming most of round 1's 1,983 ms was a harness configuration choice, not model speed.
verdicts.fails_if: >= 1,500 ms — the mini is genuinely slow and V5 stands unqualified

verdicts.prediction: Against a deliberately LONG reply, model audio keeps arriving after the vendor's interrupt signal in >=3 of 5 trials, on at least one vendor.
verdicts.fails_if: <=2 on both — the vendor stops cleanly, our playout queue has nothing left to clear, and turnManager's queue half is smaller than claimed

verdicts.prediction: At N=5 the full model's model leg p50 stays < 1,600 ms and it drops 0 turns, holding its N=1 round-1 result.
verdicts.fails_if: >= 1,600 ms or any dropped turn — the N=1 reference ceiling was luck

verdicts.prediction: On the identical 5-turn script, Gemini 2.5 native audio on Vertex costs LESS per turn than OpenAI mini ($0.00481).
verdicts.fails_if: >= $0.00481 — round 1's $0.00444 was an artefact of L5's shorter 4-turn script and the cheapest-and-fastest convergence is not real
